In this lesson, you will learn how to align the motors on the 280 Rotating Machinery trainer.
INTRODUCTIONM
The trainer is a very versatile piece of equipment.
Like many types of equipment, the trainer must be properly aligned prior to experimental use in order to obtain valid results.
Periodic alignment of the trainer should be performed to keep the trainer operating properly.
Let's begin the lesson on ROTATING MACHINERY TRAINER ALIGNMENT..............
LESSON MENU
ALIGNMENT PROCEDURES
The Rotating Machinery Trainer can be configured in a number of different ways.
DISCUSSION
Regardless of the trainers configuration, proper experiment results can only be achieved with a properly aligned trainer.
For the Model 280 to operate properly, the rotors, couplers and clutch must be properly aligned.
Misalignment will cause excessive wear on the trainer......
Misalignment will also cause incorrect measurements during experiments.
You should perform the alignment procedure before performing an experiment.
This will ensure accurate experiment results.
Misalignment usually occurs due to dropping, loose screws or clutch wear.
Misalignment can usually be checked visually...............
By looking directly down at the trainer, you can see any misalignment of the motors and couplers.
A properly aligned trainer shows a straight connection between motors and couplers.
Misalignment causes undue friction on the connecting couplers of the trainer.
Energy in the form of heat is lost in the couplers.
Misalignment also puts unneeded stress on the motors themselves.
Misaligned motor shafts generate counter torque on the motors.
This counter torque can result in premature wear on the motors.
Misalignments can be visually observed by looking at the sides of the motor shafts and couplings.
Misaligned motor shafts are not perfectly straight with each other.
Motor shafts can be aligned by adjusting the baseplates.
Misalignment can also occur due to the dynamic brake assembly.
The dynamic brake can be applied to any motor on the trainer.
If the dynamic brake is misaligned, excessive drag on the motors will occur.
The dynamic brake is controlled by the dynamic brake adjust, located on the DC motor sub-panel.
When the brake is misaligned, the brake adjust will not perform properly.
To align the dynamic brake, the mounting pad must first be adjusted.
If the dynamic brake is mounted too far away from the DC motor, the dynamic brake adjust will not work.
If the dynamic brake is mounted too close to the DC motor, the motor will lock with little or no dynamic brake adjust applied.
What is the best way of determining motor misalignments on the trainer?
The trainer can be aligned mechanically but misalignment should not be determined mechanically.

10. Carefully remove the clear plastic protective cover by removing the two allen head mounting bolts.
11. Slightly loosen the AC motor baseplate screws.
12. Carefully move the AC motor back and forth until the current meter indicates the least amount of current and maximum shaft speed.
13. While maintaining the AC Motor in position, slowly and gently tighten the AC motor baseplate screws. DO NOT OVERTIGHTEN.
Definition
14. Again, visually inspect the motor shaft couplings. Repeat the baseplate alignment for the stepper motor and DC motor, ONE AT A TIME.
Definition
If the left hand shaft coupling appears misaligned, adjust the stepper motor baseplate.
If the right hand shaft coupling appears misaligned, adjust the DC motor baseplate.
Upon completion of the motor shaft coupling alignment all motor shafts should be aligned.
If the shafts are not aligned, a shim can be inserted under the baseplate of the misaligned motor.
15. Slightly loosen the dynamic brake baseplate screws....
16. Looking straight down at the brake assembly, adjust the assembly square with the brake facing.
17. Slightly move the dynamic brake forward toward the brake faceplate until a slight abrasive sounding rasp is heard. Motor speed should slightly reduce.

Now that the 280 trainer is aligned correctly, you would think that measured values on all trainers would be the same. Not True! Motor DC Motor +24V Motor #1 1600 RPM +24V Motor #2 1600 RPM
Different motors will produce different outputs. This is not unusual.

The differences will not pose a problem. Normally, you are requested to compare readings using one trainer. Precise measurement values are important but the relationship between two values is more important...
For example, you would compare the RPM of a DC motor at different input voltages.
Even though the RPM values are different on each trainer, both trainers indicate that when input voltages increases, RPM increases.
It is the relationship between input voltage and output RPM that is important. Not the actual RPM values at different input voltages.
